\[
c = \bigl[(A^{\mathsf T} A)^{-1} A^{\mathsf T}\bigr]_{0},
\qquad
A_{ij} = (i - m)^j,
\qquad
I_{\text{out}} = c \ast_{x} (c \ast_{y} I)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(c\): The smoothing weights
- \(A\): The matrix of powers of the positions
- \(m\): The center position, (n - 1) / 2
- \(p\): The polynomial degree

A has one row per window position i, from 0 to n - 1, and one column per power j, from 0 to p. m = (n - 1) / 2 is the center. The least-squares fit of a polynomial to the window values y has coefficients (A^T A)^-1 A^T y. Its value at the center is the first coefficient, so the weights c are the first row of that matrix. They do not depend on the data, so the filter is a fixed kernel. It runs along rows, then along columns.
